record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.context_brief: Nuclear DIS effects in gamma-W-box corrections
record.original_question: How do nuclear shadowing and EMC modifications of the parity-violating deep-inelastic-scattering structure function F3 affect nuclear gamma-W-box radiative corrections, and do the cancellations found in the Gross-Llewellyn-Smith sum rule survive in models beyond the initial studies?

evidence.quote: It is well-known, however, that the DIS nuclear structure functions typically show shadowing and EMC effects (139, 140).
Experimentally, this has been studied predominantly for the parity-conserving structure function F2 (141, 142, 143) rather than the parity-violating function F3 entering ∆ V R.

Initial studies on F3 showed strong effects on the structure function but found large cancellations in the Gross-Llewellyn-Smith sum rule (144). To leading twist the latter informs the DIS contribution to ∆ V R, but it is not clear whether the same conclusion is reached in other models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the parity-violating deep-inelastic-scattering (DIS) structure function $F_3(x, Q^2)$ of a nucleon bound in a nucleus, and let $F_3^A(x, Q^2)$ denote its nuclear analogue. It is empirically established (primarily for the parity-conserving structure function $F_2$) that nuclear structure functions exhibit shadowing at small Bjorken $x$ and EMC-type suppression at intermediate $x$, so that $F_2^A/(A F_2^N) \neq 1$. The Gross–Llewellyn-Smith (GLS) sum rule relates the lowest odd moment of $F_3$ to the valence quark number,
$$\mathrm{GLS}(Q^2) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{x}\bigl[F_3^{\nu N}(x,Q^2) + F_3^{\bar\nu N}(x,Q^2)\bigr] = 3\bigl[1 + \text{(perturbative and higher-twist corrections)}\bigr].$$
At leading twist, this sum rule controls the DIS contribution to the universal electroweak radiative correction $\Delta_V^R$ arising from the $\gamma W$-box diagram in semileptonic charged-current processes; the nuclear analogue determines the corresponding nuclear $\gamma W$-box correction relevant to superallowed $\beta$ decays.

Problem. Quantify the effect of nuclear shadowing and EMC-type modifications of $F_3$ on the nuclear $\gamma W$-box radiative correction. In particular, determine whether the strong cancellations between shadowing and EMC contributions to the nuclear GLS integral, observed in initial model studies, persist across a broad class of nuclear models (Glauber–Gribov multiple scattering, vector meson dominance, color-dipole / saturation models, convolution / nucleon off-shell models, and any other reasonable framework). Provide either a model-independent argument that such cancellations survive (and hence that the nuclear correction to the $\gamma W$-box from these effects is bounded by some small explicit number), or exhibit a model in which the cancellation is significantly violated and estimate the resulting shift in $\Delta_V^R$ for nuclei of phenomenological interest.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., 2025 high-precision determinations of radiative corrections to superallowed nuclear β decays, and 2025 lattice QCD studies of the GLS sum rule) continues to investigate nuclear DIS modifications of F3 and γW-box corrections; no model-independent demonstration that the EMC/shadowing cancellations in the nuclear GLS integral hold across all nuclear models has been established. The question therefore appears still open.

status_evidence.title: High-precision determination of radiative corrections to superallowed nuclear beta decays
status_evidence.snippet: Nuclear contributions to parity-odd structure functions F3 include nuclear modifications such as shadowing, antishadowing and the EMC effect; treated within Glauber-Gribov approaches.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 the treatment of nuclear shadowing/EMC effects in F3 for γW-box corrections is still being refined model-by-model.

status_evidence.title: Gross-Llewellyn Smith sum rule from lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice QCD evaluation of the GLS sum rule with implications for higher-twist effects and electroweak box contributions for CKM unitarity.
status_evidence.claim: The GLS-based input to ΔVR remains under active study, with model dependence not fully resolved.
